claims.statement: MDR requires a continuous post-market surveillance system and periodic safety update reports for Class IIa/IIb devices, including sales or usage denominators and benefit-risk conclusions.
Current MDCG guidance connects complaints, service information, exposure, trend thresholds, risk management and CAPA, supporting a real cross-source traceability job.
MDCG's PSUR guidance provides a systematic template and cadence but does not make an external software vendor a mandatory control point.
A qualified PRRC and manufacturer personnel must retain regulatory compliance authority; the founder cannot substitute software for those qualifications.
Serious incident reporting can run on two-, ten- or fifteen-day clocks, so founder-only support would be incompatible with critical reporting operations.
EUDAMED's PMS and vigilance module remains under development even though four other modules became mandatory in May 2026, leaving workflow gaps but no exclusive platform gate.
MasterControl and Greenlight Guru already market integrated post-market, complaint, risk, CAPA and reporting workflows, creating direct bundling pressure.
Complaint records may contain health data, requiring a lawful GDPR basis, minimization, security and clear controller-processor responsibilities rather than unrestricted model training.

Europe has more than 38,000 medical-technology companies and roughly 90% are SMEs, but that broad statistic does not establish the reachable Class IIa/IIb segment or a conservative customer denominator.
The candidate earns a distinct budget only if a paid pilot shows faster, more complete complaint-to-denominator-to-risk-to-PSUR lineage than incumbent QMS/PMS suites and consultant workarounds.

contrary_evidence: Established QMS vendors already bundle complaints, PMS, risk, CAPA and regulatory reporting.
MDCG templates and regulatory duties create a required artifact, not an exclusive vendor-controlled gate.
Qualified customer personnel retain safety, reportability and approval authority.
EUDAMED module evolution may absorb portions of the workflow.
Generic AI extraction and drafting are reproducible and cannot alone support defensibility.

economics.acquisition_route: Founder-led fixed-fee traceability assessments for the first two customers, then independent QA/RA consultant referrals; conversion, referral economics and CAC are unknown.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative rather than validated: 175 customers at PLN 60,000 ARR equals PLN 10.5m ARR; at 25% normalized earnings, 80% founder ownership and a 3x earnings value, founder equity is about PLN 6.3m. Reaching this in 8-10 years requires proof of price, retention, service leverage and a reachable pool; the 38,000-plus European medtech firms and 90% SME statistic is only a broad denominator.
economics.founder_time: At most five hours daily while employed, capped initially at two design partners; contract qualified QA/RA and validation help, keep regulatory reporting with the customer, and establish an escalation rotation independent of the founder.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Estimated 55-70% gross margin during implementation-heavy early years and 70-80% only after connectors, validation artifacts and support are standardized; qualified QA/RA review remains customer-paid or explicitly passed through.
economics.payback: Onboarding should cover configuration and validation labor, while recurring gross profit should repay acquisition cost within 12 months; sales-cycle duration and actual CAC remain unknown.
economics.pricing: Test PLN 15,000-50,000 for scoped onboarding and validation plus PLN 1,500-6,000 per month per manufacturer; these remain unvalidated assumptions and must be tested against bundled QMS/PMS alternatives.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Continuous PMS and periodic PSUR duties support recurring use, but retention is threatened by QMS-suite consolidation, consultant-led workarounds and customer insourcing.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Customer-specific validated lineage rules and, with lawful permission, de-identified mappings of complaint patterns to evidence requests could improve implementation, but health-data limits, validation burden, incumbent suites and reproducible AI extraction sharply constrain this advantage.
fingerprint.customer: Small EU Class IIa/IIb medical-device manufacturers managing roughly 1-20 device families with lean QA/RA teams and fragmented complaint, service, exposure and risk evidence.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: A fixed-fee complaint-to-PSUR traceability assessment followed by software conversion, supplemented by referrals from independent QA/RA consultants; no signed channel or conversion evidence exists.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Validated SaaS for controlled intake, deduplication, trend and denominator workpapers, risk/CAPA linking, PSUR drafting, qualified sign-off and audit exports, sold through onboarding plus subscription; it does not autonomously decide safety, reportability or regulatory submissions.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The manufacturer's head of QA/RA or quality leader pays an annual software license plus validated onboarding when fragmented evidence and recurring PSUR work justify a controlled system; actual willingness to pay is unknown.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A complaint, service signal, periodic review or PSUR due date exposes incomplete traceability from raw post-market evidence through trend denominators, vigilance assessment, risk/CAPA actions and the approved report.

founder_fit: The founder's data-science and health interests fit entity resolution, signal normalization, trend workpapers and evidence retrieval.
A narrow evidence-lineage product is feasible alongside employment only if it avoids device-safety judgment and supports a small number of high-value customers.
The founder is not established as a qualified PRRC or regulatory professional, so qualified customer or contracted QA/RA personnel must own regulated conclusions and validation.
Two-, ten- and fifteen-day vigilance clocks require customer-owned reporting and an independent support escalation path rather than founder-only availability.
risks: Incumbent bundling makes the product a feature rather than a company.
Services-heavy validation and ontology work prevent software gross margins.
Health and complaint data increase privacy, security and contractual liability.
Customers may mistakenly rely on automation for non-delegable regulatory judgments.
Founder availability cannot cover vigilance-critical incidents without independent operations.
An unsupported broad SME denominator could overstate the founder wealth path.

structure.commercial_archetype: High-trust regulated evidence SaaS with paid validation and onboarding
structure.control_point: The auditable lineage from source complaint or service evidence through exposure denominator and trend analysis to risk/CAPA disposition, qualified approval and PSUR output.
structure.critical_dependency: Complete customer data, validated software and security controls, plus qualified PRRC/QA/RA personnel at the customer who retain safety, reportability, submission and approval authority.

thesis: A controlled evidence workbench can help small Class IIa/IIb manufacturers continuously connect complaints, service records, literature and exposure denominators to vigilance assessment, risk management, CAPA and PSUR drafting. MDR and MDCG guidance establish the recurring cross-source traceability job, but QMS/PMS incumbents already bundle much of it; a distinct paid control point exists only if the product proves materially deeper complaint-to-denominator-to-risk-to-PSUR lineage while qualified customer personnel retain every safety, reportability and approval decision.
title: MDR Complaint-to-PSUR Evidence Workbench
uncertainties: Paid willingness to adopt a separate traceability layer rather than an incumbent QMS module
Representative complaint volume, data fragmentation and PSUR preparation hours
Validated reduction in review time, missing links and audit findings
Integration and software-validation burden per customer
Consultant channel commitment, CAC, sales cycle and churn
Reachable count of small EU Class IIa/IIb manufacturers with the relevant pain
